**Tafsir (exegesis) of Surat al-Talaq**

It is a Medinan surah.

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

* *

The Prophet (ﷺ) was addressed first, as an honour and a mark of distinction, and then he addressed the Ummah (the community) by extension, saying: ﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them at their prescribed waiting period﴾.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Thawab ibn Sa'id al-Hubari narrated to us, Asbat ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) divorced Hafsah, and she went to her family. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them at their prescribed waiting period﴾. It was said to him: "Take her back, for she fasts often and prays much at night, and she is one of your wives in Paradise."

Ibn Jarir related it from Ibn Bashshar, from Abd al-A'la, from Sa'id, from Qatadah... and he mentioned it as a mursal report [[Tafsir al-Tabari (28/85)]]. It has also come through other routes that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) divorced Hafsah and then took her back.

Al-Bukhari said: Yahya ibn Bukayr narrated to us, al-Layth and Uqayl narrated to us, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Salim informed me that Abdullah ibn Umar informed him that he divorced his wife while she was menstruating. Umar mentioned this to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) became angry, then said: "Let him take her back, then keep her until she becomes pure, then she menstruates and becomes pure again. If he then wishes to divorce her, let him divorce her while she is pure and before he has had intercourse with her. That is the waiting period which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has commanded" [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4908)]].

Thus al-Bukhari narrated it here, and he narrated it in other places in his book. Muslim also narrated it, and his wording is: "That is the waiting period which Allah has commanded for women to be divorced in."[[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (5251) and Sahih Muslim, no. (1471)]]

It was also narrated by the compilers of the books and the musnads (collections arranged by narrator) through many routes and with many wordings [[Al-Musnad (2/26, 43, 51, 54, 58), Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (2179), Sunan al-Nasa'i (6/138), and Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (2023)]]. The places where it is fully examined are the books of legal rulings.

The wording most closely related to the verse here is what Muslim narrated in his Sahih by way of Ibn Jurayj: Abu al-Zubayr informed me that he heard Abd al-Rahman ibn Ayman, the freedman of Azzah, asking Ibn Umar, while Abu al-Zubayr was listening: "What is your opinion regarding a man who divorced his wife while she was menstruating?" He said: "Ibn Umar divorced his wife while she was menstruating during the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Umar asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about it, and said: 'Abdullah ibn Umar divorced his wife while she was menstruating.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Let him take her back.' So he took her back, and he said: 'When she becomes pure, let him either divorce her or keep her.'" Ibn Umar said: The Prophet (ﷺ) recited: ﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them at their prescribed waiting period﴾ [[Sahih Muslim, no. (14719)]].

Al-A'mash said, from Malik ibn al-Harith, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid, from Abdullah (ibn Mas'ud), regarding His words: ﴿divorce them at their prescribed waiting period﴾, that he said: "It is the purity period without intercourse" [[Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (28/83)]]. The same has been reported from Ibn Umar, Ata', Mujahid, al-Hasan, Ibn Sirin, Qatadah, Maymun ibn Mihran, and Muqatil ibn Hayyan. It is also a narration from Ikrimah and al-Dahhak.

Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words, Exalted is He: ﴿divorce them at their prescribed waiting period﴾, that he said: "He should not divorce her while she is menstruating, nor in a purity period in which he has had intercourse with her. Rather, he should leave her until she menstruates and becomes pure, then divorce her with one pronouncement."

Ikrimah said: ﴿divorce them at their prescribed waiting period﴾: "The waiting period is the purity period, and the qur' (menstrual cycle, a term used for both purity and menstruation) is the menstruation. It means that he divorces her when she is pregnant and her pregnancy is clear, and he does not divorce her after he has had intercourse with her and does not know whether she is pregnant or not."

From this point the jurists (fuqaha') derived the rulings on divorce and divided it into *talaq al-sunnah* (divorce in accordance with the Sunnah, the prophetic way) and *talaq al-bid'ah* (innovative divorce, contrary to the Sunnah). Divorce in accordance with the Sunnah is that he divorces her while she is in a state of purity without intercourse, or while she is pregnant and her pregnancy is clear. Innovative divorce is that he divorces her during menstruation, or in a purity period in which he has had intercourse with her, and he does not know whether she has conceived or not. There is also a third type of divorce that is neither Sunnah nor innovation: the divorce of a young girl, of a woman past menopause, and of a woman who has not been consummated. The detailed discussion of this and what relates to it is fully covered in the books of jurisprudence (furu'), and Allah, Glorified and Exalted, knows best.

* *

His words: ﴿And count the waiting period﴾ mean: preserve it, and know its beginning and its end, so that the waiting period does not extend over the woman, causing her to refrain from marrying. ﴿And fear Allah, your Lord﴾ means: in that matter.

* *

His words: ﴿Do not turn them out of their houses, nor should they leave﴾ mean: during the waiting period she has the right to lodging from the husband for as long as she is in the waiting period from him. So the man has no right to expel her, and it is also not permissible for her to leave, because she is bound (*mu'takalah*) [[In manuscript A: "mutaʿallaqah" (attached)]] to the husband's right as well.

* *

His words: ﴿Unless they commit a clear immorality﴾ mean: they should not leave their houses except that the woman commits a clear immorality, in which case she may leave the house. The clear immorality includes fornication, as stated by Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn Abbas, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, al-Sha'bi, al-Hasan, Ibn Sirin, Mujahid, Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Abu Qilabah, Abu Salih, al-Dahhak, Zayd ibn Aslam, Ata' al-Khurasani, al-Suddi, Sa'id ibn Abi Hilal, and others. It also includes whether the woman becomes disobedient (*nashazat*) or behaves badly towards the husband's family and harms them in speech and deeds, as stated by Ubayy ibn Ka'b, Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, and others.

* *

His words: ﴿Those are the limits of Allah﴾ mean: His laws and His prohibitions. ﴿And whoever transgresses the limits of Allah﴾ means: goes beyond them, exceeds them, and does not comply with them. ﴿Then he has wronged himself﴾ means: by doing that.

* *

His words: ﴿You know not; perhaps Allah will bring about after that some matter﴾ mean: We only kept the divorced woman in the husband's home during the waiting period, perhaps the husband will regret his divorce of her, and Allah will place in his heart the desire to take her back, and that would be easier and simpler.

Al-Zuhri said, from Ubayd Allah ibn Abd Allah, from Fatimah bint Qays, regarding His words: ﴿You know not; perhaps Allah will bring about after that some matter﴾: "It is the reconciliation (*al-raj'ah*)." Likewise said al-Sha'bi, Ata', Qatadah, al-Dahhak, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, and al-Thawri.

From this point, some of the early scholars (salaf) and those who followed them went to the view, such as the Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal, may Allah have mercy on him, that lodging is not obligatory for a woman who has been irrevocably divorced (*mabtutah*), and likewise for a widow. They also relied on the hadith of Fatimah bint Qays al-Fihriyyah, when her husband Abu Amr ibn Hafs divorced her with the last of three pronouncements while he was absent from her in Yemen. He sent her word of this, and sent her agent with barley as maintenance, and she was angered by it. He said: "By Allah, you have no maintenance from us." She went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said: "You have no maintenance from him." In Muslim's version: "Nor lodging." He ordered her to observe her waiting period in the house of Umm Shurayk, then he said: "That is a woman whom my companions visit. Observe your waiting period at the house of Ibn Umm Maktum, for he is a blind man, and you may put off your clothes." The hadith [[Sahih Muslim, no. (1480)]].

Imam Ahmad narrated it by another route with different wording, saying:

Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, Mujalid narrated to us, Amir narrated to us, who said: I came to Madinah and visited Fatimah bint Qays, and she told me that her husband divorced her during the time of the Prophet (ﷺ), and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent him on an expedition. She said: "His brother said to me: 'Leave the house.' I said: 'I have maintenance and lodging until the term ends.' He said: 'No.' So I came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: 'So-and-so divorced me, and his brother has expelled me and denied me lodging and maintenance.' [So he sent for him]. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'What is the matter with you and the daughter of Al Qays?' He said: 'O Messenger of Allah, my brother divorced her three times at once.' She said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Consider, O daughter of Al Qays: maintenance and lodging are only due to the woman from her husband if he has the right of reconciliation over her. If he does not have the right of reconciliation over her, then there is no maintenance and no lodging. Go and stay with so-and-so.'" Then he said: "She is spoken to, so stay with Ibn Umm Maktum, for he is blind and cannot see you," and he mentioned the rest of the hadith [[Al-Musnad (6/373)]].

Al-Tabarani, Abu al-Qasim, said: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Bazzar al-Tustari narrated to us, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Sawwaf narrated to us, Bakr ibn Bakkar narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Yazid al-Bajali narrated to us, Amir al-Sha'bi narrated to us: that he entered upon Fatimah bint Qays, sister of al-Dahhak ibn Qays al-Qurashi, whose husband was Abu Amr ibn Hafs ibn al-Mughirah al-Makhzumi. She said: "Abu Amr ibn Hafs sent to me, while he was setting out with an army to Yemen, with my divorce. I asked his guardians for maintenance and lodging for me, and they said: 'He did not send anything to us about that, nor did he instruct us regarding it.' So I went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, Abu Amr ibn Hafs sent to me with my divorce, and I asked for lodging and maintenance.' His guardians said: 'He did not send us anything about that.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Maintenance and lodging are only due to the woman when her husband has the right of reconciliation over her. If she is not lawful to him until she marries another husband, then she has no maintenance and no lodging.'"

Likewise al-Nasa'i narrated it [[Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (24/382) and Sunan al-Nasa'i (6/144)]], from Ahmad ibn Yahya al-Sufi, from Abu Nu'aym al-Fadl ibn Dukayn, from Sa'id ibn Yazid, who is al-Ahmasi al-Bajali al-Kufi. Abu Hatim al-Razi said: "He is a shaykh (elderly scholar) from whom narrations are transmitted" [[Al-Jarh wa al-Ta'dil by Ibn Abi Hatim (4/74)]].

The Most High says: ﴿So when they [the divorced women] have reached their term﴾, meaning they have come close to completing the 'iddah (the waiting period) and are near to it, but the 'iddah has not yet been fully finished. At that point, either the husband resolves to retain her, which means taking her back into the bond of marriage and continuing with her as she was with him, ﴿in kindness﴾, meaning treating her well in his companionship with her. Or he resolves to part from her ﴿in kindness﴾, meaning without reviling, abusing or reproaching her, but divorcing her in a fair manner and a good way.

* *

His saying: ﴿And call to witness two just men from among you﴾, meaning to witness the taking back (of the wife) if you resolve upon it, as Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah narrated from Imran [[In M: "Amr"]] ibn Husayn, that he was asked about a man who divorces his wife, then has intercourse with her, and did not call witnesses to her divorce or to her taking back. He said: "You divorced her in a way not sanctioned, and you took her back in a way not sanctioned. Call witnesses to her divorce and to her taking back, and do not return [to that]." [[In A: "and do not ta'tad"]] [[Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 2186, and Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 2025.]]

Ibn Juraij said: Ata' used to say: ﴿And call to witness two just men from among you﴾. He said: It is not permissible in marriage, divorce or taking back except with two just witnesses, as Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has said, unless there is an excuse.

* *

His saying: ﴿That is admonished by it whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day﴾, meaning: this which We have commanded you concerning calling witnesses and establishing testimony is only heeded by whoever believes in Allah and that He legislated this, and fears the punishment of Allah in the Hereafter.

From here, al-Shafi'i, in one of his two opinions, held that calling witnesses for the taking back is obligatory, just as it is obligatory in his view at the beginning of a marriage. A group of scholars held this view, and whoever holds it says that the taking back is not valid except by speech, so that witnessing may take place upon it.

* *

His saying: ﴿And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out and provide for him from where he does not expect﴾, meaning: whoever fears Allah regarding what He has commanded him and abandons what He has forbidden him, Allah will make for him a way out from his affair, and will provide for him from where he does not expect, meaning from a source that does not occur to his mind.

Imam Ahmad said: Yazid narrated to us, Kahmas ibn al-Hasan informed us, Abu al-Salil narrated to us, from Abu Dharr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) began reciting to me this verse: ﴿And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out and provide for him from where he does not expect﴾, until he finished the verse. Then he said: "O Abu Dharr, if all the people took hold of it, it would suffice them." He said: He kept reciting it and repeating it to me until I became drowsy. Then he said: "O Abu Dharr, what will you do if you are expelled from Madinah?" I said: "I will go to ease and comfort, and I will be a dove among the doves of Makkah." He said: "What will you do if you are expelled from Makkah?" He said: I said: "To ease and comfort, and to Syria, the Holy Land." He said: "And what will you do if you are expelled from Syria?" I said: "Then, by Him who sent you with the truth, I will place my sword upon my shoulder." He said: "Is there something better than that?" I said: "Is there something better than that?" He said: "Hear and obey, even if he is an Abyssinian slave."[[Al-Musnad (5/178).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Ramadi narrated to us, Ya'la ibn Ubayd narrated to us, Zakariyya narrated to us, from Amir, from Shutayr [[In A: "from Bisr"]] ibn Shakal, who said: I heard Abdullah ibn Mas'ud say: "The most comprehensive verse in the Qur'an is: ﴿Indeed, Allah commands justice and good conduct﴾ [al-Nahl: 90], and the verse in the Qur'an most full of relief is: ﴿And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out﴾."

In the Musnad: Mahdi ibn Ja'far narrated to me, al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, from al-Hakam ibn Mus'ab, from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Abdullah ibn Abbas, from his father, from his grandfather Abdullah ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever frequently seeks forgiveness, Allah will make for him a relief from every distress, a way out from every constriction, and will provide for him from where he does not expect."[[Al-Musnad (1/248).]]

Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out﴾, meaning: He will deliver him from every calamity in this world and the Hereafter. ﴿And provide for him from where he does not expect﴾.

Al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym said: ﴿He will make for him a way out﴾, meaning: from everything that constricts upon people.

Ikrimah said: Whoever divorces as Allah commanded, He will make for him a way out. Likewise it was narrated from Ibn Abbas and al-Dahhak.

Ibn Mas'ud and Masruq said: ﴿And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out﴾: he knows that Allah, if He wills, withholds, and if He wills, gives. ﴿From where he does not expect﴾, meaning [[In M: "or"]] from where he does not know.

Qatadah said: ﴿And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out﴾, meaning: from the doubtful matters and from distress at the time of death. ﴿And provide for him from where he does not expect﴾, and from where he does not hope or anticipate.

Al-Suddi said: ﴿And whoever fears Allah﴾ divorces according to the Sunnah, and takes back according to the Sunnah. He claimed that a man from among the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), called "Awf ibn Malik al-Ashja'i," had a son, and that the polytheists captured him, and he was among them. His father would come to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and complain to him about the place of his son and his condition and his need. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would command him to be patient, and would say to him: "Indeed Allah will make for you a relief." [[In M, A: "a way out."]] Not long after that, his son escaped from the hands of the enemy and passed by a flock of sheep belonging to the enemy, so he drove them off and brought them to his father, and brought with him a booty [[In M: "a gain"]] of sheep he had obtained. So this verse was revealed concerning him: ﴿And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out and provide for him from where he does not expect﴾.

Ibn Jarir narrated it.[[Tafsir al-Tabari (28/89).]] It was also narrated through the route of Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd as a mursal report, similar to it.[[Tafsir al-Tabari (28/90). It has also come as a connected report, narrated by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak (2/492) through the route of Ubayd ibn Kathir al-Amiri, from Abbad ibn Ya'qub, from Yahya ibn Adam, from Isra'il, from Ammar ibn Abi Mu'awiyah, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, from Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: This verse was revealed... and he mentioned something similar to the narration of al-Suddi. Al-Hakim said: "Its chain is sound, but they did not record it." Al-Dhahabi criticised him, saying: "Rather it is munkar; in it is Abbad ibn Ya'qub, an extreme Rafidi, and Ubayd ibn Kathir al-Amiri, who is abandoned, as stated by al-Azdi."]]

Imam Ahmad said: Waki' narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn Isa, from Abdullah ibn Abi al-Ja'd, from Thawban, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed a servant is deprived of provision because of a sin he commits, and nothing turns away decree except supplication, and nothing increases lifespan except righteousness."

Al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah also narrated it from the hadith of Sufyan, who is al-Thawri, with this chain.[[Al-Musnad (5/277) and Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 4022.]]

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Malik al-Ashja'i came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "My son Awf has been captured." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "Send word to him that the Messenger of Allah commands you to recite much: There is no power and no strength except with Allah." The captors had bound him with rawhide, and the rawhide fell from him. He went out, and behold, there was a camel of theirs, so he mounted it and turned back. Then he saw the herd of the people who had bound him, so he shouted at them, and the first of them followed the last. He did not surprise his parents except that he was calling at the door. His father said: "Awf, by the Lord of the Ka'bah!" His mother said: "Woe to us!" [She asked:] "How could Awf come while he is in the rawhide?" They raced to the door and the servant, and behold, Awf had filled the courtyard with camels. He related to his father his affair and the affair of the camels. His father said: "Wait until I come to the Messenger of Allah and ask him about them." He came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and informed him of the news of Awf and the news of the camels. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "Do with them whatever you wish, just as you would do with your own property." And this was revealed: ﴿And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out and provide for him from where he does not expect﴾.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Shaqiq narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn al-Ash'ath narrated to us, al-Fudayl ibn Iyad narrated to us, from Hisham ibn Hassan [[In M, A, H: "al-Hasan," taken from the margin of the Shaʿb edition.]], from Imran ibn Husayn, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever devotes himself to Allah, Allah will suffice him for every burden, and provide for him from where he does not expect. And whoever devotes himself to the world, Allah will leave him to it."[[Also narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Saghir (1/116), and from him al-Khatib in his Tarikh (7/197), through the route of Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Baghdadi, from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Shaqiq with this chain. Al-Tabarani said: "No one narrated it from Hisham except al-Fudayl; Ibrahim ibn al-Ash'ath is the sole narrator of it." Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/304): "In its chain is Ibrahim ibn al-Ash'ath, the companion of al-Fudayl, and he is weak. Ibn Hibban mentioned him among the trustworthy and said: He is strange, errs and contradicts, and the rest of its narrators are trustworthy."]]

* *

His saying: ﴿And whoever relies upon Allah, then He is sufficient for him﴾. Imam Ahmad said:

Yunus narrated to us, Layth narrated to us, Qays ibn al-Hajjaj narrated to us, from Hannash al-San'ani, from Abdullah ibn Abbas, that he related to him that he once rode behind the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "O boy, I will teach you some words: Guard Allah and He will guard you. Guard Allah and you will find Him before you. If you ask, ask Allah, and if you seek help, seek help from Allah. Know that if the nation were to gather together to benefit you, they would not benefit you except with something Allah has written for you; and if they gathered together to harm you, they would not harm you except with something Allah has written against you. The pens have been lifted and the pages have dried."

Al-Tirmidhi narrated it through the hadith of al-Layth ibn Sa'd and Ibn Lahi'ah, with this chain, and he said: "Hasan sahih."[[Al-Musnad (1/293) and Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 2326.]]

Imam Ahmad said: Waki' narrated to us, Bishr ibn Salman narrated to us, from Sayyar Abu al-Hakam, from Tariq ibn Shihab, from Abdullah, that is Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever has a need and brings it to people, it is likely that his need will not be easily fulfilled. And whoever brings it to Allah, Allah will bring him provision quickly, or death in its appointed time."

He then narrated it from Abdal-Razzaq, from Sufyan, from Bishr, from Sayyar Abu Hamzah. Then he said: "And this is the correct version, and Sayyar Abu al-Hakam did not narrate from Tariq."[[Al-Musnad (1/442).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Ramadi narrated to us, Ya'la ibn Ubayd narrated to us, Zakariyya narrated to us, from Amir, from Shutayr [[In A: "from Bisr"]] ibn Shakal, who said: I heard Abdullah ibn Mas'ud say: "The most comprehensive verse in the Qur'an is: ﴿Indeed, Allah commands justice and good conduct﴾ [al-Nahl: 90], and the verse in the Qur'an most full of relief is: ﴿And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out﴾."

In the Musnad: Mahdi ibn Ja'far narrated to me, al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, from al-Hakam ibn Mus'ab, from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Abdullah ibn Abbas, from his father, from his grandfather Abdullah ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever frequently seeks forgiveness, Allah will make for him a relief from every distress, a way out from every constriction, and will provide for him from where he does not expect."[[Al-Musnad (1/248).]]

Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out﴾, meaning: He will deliver him from every calamity in this world and the Hereafter. ﴿And provide for him from where he does not expect﴾.

Al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym said: ﴿He will make for him a way out﴾, meaning: from everything that constricts upon people.

Ikrimah said: Whoever divorces as Allah commanded, He will make for him a way out. Likewise it was narrated from Ibn Abbas and al-Dahhak.

Ibn Mas'ud and Masruq said: ﴿And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out﴾: he knows that Allah, if He wills, withholds, and if He wills, gives. ﴿From where he does not expect﴾, meaning [[In M: "or"]] from where he does not know.

Qatadah said: ﴿And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out﴾, meaning: from the doubtful matters and from distress at the time of death. ﴿And provide for him from where he does not expect﴾, and from where he does not hope or anticipate.

Al-Suddi said: ﴿And whoever fears Allah﴾ divorces according to the Sunnah, and takes back according to the Sunnah. He claimed that a man from among the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), called "Awf ibn Malik al-Ashja'i," had a son, and that the polytheists captured him, and he was among them. His father would come to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and complain to him about the place of his son and his condition and his need. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would command him to be patient, and would say to him: "Indeed Allah will make for you a relief." [[In M, A: "a way out."]] Not long after that, his son escaped from the hands of the enemy and passed by a flock of sheep belonging to the enemy, so he drove them off and brought them to his father, and brought with him a booty [[In M: "a gain"]] of sheep he had obtained. So this verse was revealed concerning him: ﴿And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out and provide for him from where he does not expect﴾.

Ibn Jarir narrated it.[[Tafsir al-Tabari (28/89).]] It was also narrated through the route of Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd as a mursal report, similar to it.[[Tafsir al-Tabari (28/90). It has also come as a connected report, narrated by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak (2/492) through the route of Ubayd ibn Kathir al-Amiri, from Abbad ibn Ya'qub, from Yahya ibn Adam, from Isra'il, from Ammar ibn Abi Mu'awiyah, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, from Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: This verse was revealed... and he mentioned something similar to the narration of al-Suddi. Al-Hakim said: "Its chain is sound, but they did not record it." Al-Dhahabi criticised him, saying: "Rather it is munkar; in it is Abbad ibn Ya'qub, an extreme Rafidi, and Ubayd ibn Kathir al-Amiri, who is abandoned, as stated by al-Azdi."]]

Imam Ahmad said: Waki' narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn Isa, from Abdullah ibn Abi al-Ja'd, from Thawban, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed a servant is deprived of provision because of a sin he commits, and nothing turns away decree except supplication, and nothing increases lifespan except righteousness."

Al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah also narrated it from the hadith of Sufyan, who is al-Thawri, with this chain.[[Al-Musnad (5/277) and Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 4022.]]

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Malik al-Ashja'i came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "My son Awf has been captured." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "Send word to him that the Messenger of Allah commands you to recite much: There is no power and no strength except with Allah." The captors had bound him with rawhide, and the rawhide fell from him. He went out, and behold, there was a camel of theirs, so he mounted it and turned back. Then he saw the herd of the people who had bound him, so he shouted at them, and the first of them followed the last. He did not surprise his parents except that he was calling at the door. His father said: "Awf, by the Lord of the Ka'bah!" His mother said: "Woe to us!" [She asked:] "How could Awf come while he is in the rawhide?" They raced to the door and the servant, and behold, Awf had filled the courtyard with camels. He related to his father his affair and the affair of the camels. His father said: "Wait until I come to the Messenger of Allah and ask him about them." He came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and informed him of the news of Awf and the news of the camels. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "Do with them whatever you wish, just as you would do with your own property." And this was revealed: ﴿And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out and provide for him from where he does not expect﴾.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Shaqiq narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn al-Ash'ath narrated to us, al-Fudayl ibn Iyad narrated to us, from Hisham ibn Hassan [[In M, A, H: "al-Hasan," taken from the margin of the Shaʿb edition.]], from Imran ibn Husayn, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever devotes himself to Allah, Allah will suffice him for every burden, and provide for him from where he does not expect. And whoever devotes himself to the world, Allah will leave him to it."[[Also narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Saghir (1/116), and from him al-Khatib in his Tarikh (7/197), through the route of Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Baghdadi, from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Shaqiq with this chain. Al-Tabarani said: "No one narrated it from Hisham except al-Fudayl; Ibrahim ibn al-Ash'ath is the sole narrator of it." Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/304): "In its chain is Ibrahim ibn al-Ash'ath, the companion of al-Fudayl, and he is weak. Ibn Hibban mentioned him among the trustworthy and said: He is strange, errs and contradicts, and the rest of its narrators are trustworthy."]]

* *

His saying: ﴿And whoever relies upon Allah, then He is sufficient for him﴾. Imam Ahmad said:

Yunus narrated to us, Layth narrated to us, Qays ibn al-Hajjaj narrated to us, from Hannash al-San'ani, from Abdullah ibn Abbas, that he related to him that he once rode behind the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "O boy, I will teach you some words: Guard Allah and He will guard you. Guard Allah and you will find Him before you. If you ask, ask Allah, and if you seek help, seek help from Allah. Know that if the nation were to gather together to benefit you, they would not benefit you except with something Allah has written for you; and if they gathered together to harm you, they would not harm you except with something Allah has written against you. The pens have been lifted and the pages have dried."

Al-Tirmidhi narrated it through the hadith of al-Layth ibn Sa'd and Ibn Lahi'ah, with this chain, and he said: "Hasan sahih."[[Al-Musnad (1/293) and Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 2326.]]

Imam Ahmad said: Waki' narrated to us, Bishr ibn Salman narrated to us, from Sayyar Abu al-Hakam, from Tariq ibn Shihab, from Abdullah, that is Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever has a need and brings it to people, it is likely that his need will not be easily fulfilled. And whoever brings it to Allah, Allah will bring him provision quickly, or death in its appointed time."

He then narrated it from Abdal-Razzaq, from Sufyan, from Bishr, from Sayyar Abu Hamzah. Then he said: "And this is the correct version, and Sayyar Abu al-Hakam did not narrate from Tariq."[[Al-Musnad (1/442).]]

* *

His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah will accomplish His purpose﴾, meaning: He will carry out His decrees and judgments among His creation as He wills and desires. ﴿Allah has already set for everything a destiny﴾, like His saying: ﴿And everything with Him is in measure﴾ [al-Ra'd: 8].

Ibn Kathir said, explaining the 'idda (waiting period) of the woman who has passed menopause, meaning the one whose menses have stopped due to old age: her waiting period is three months, in place of the three menstrual cycles (quru') for the woman who menstruates, as the verse of al-Baqarah [[That is verse 228.]] also indicates. Likewise, the young girls who have not yet reached the age of menstruation: their waiting period is like that of the woman past menopause, three months. This is why He said: ﴿And those who have not yet menstruated [likewise]﴾.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿if you are in doubt﴾, there are two opinions:

The first, which is the view of a group of the early scholars, such as Mujahid, al-Zuhri and Ibn Zayd: that is, if they see blood and you are uncertain whether it is menstruation or irregular bleeding (istihadah), and you are in doubt about it.

The second opinion: if you are in doubt about the ruling on their waiting period and do not know it, then it is three months. This is narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr. It is the choice of Ibn Jarir, and it is more apparent in meaning. He supported it with what he narrated from Abu Kurayb and Abu al-Sa'ib, who both said: Ibn Idris related to us, Mutarrif informed us, from Amr ibn Salim, who said: Ubayy ibn Ka'b said: "O Messenger of Allah, there are some categories of women's waiting periods that are not mentioned in the Book: the young, the old, and those who are pregnant." He said: Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And those of your women who have despaired of menstruation, if you are in doubt, their waiting period is three months, and those who have not menstruated; and for those who are pregnant, their term is until they deliver their burden﴾.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it in a fuller form than this context, saying: My father related to us, Yahya ibn al-Mughirah related to us, Jarir informed us, from Mutarrif, from Umar [[In A: "from Amr".]] ibn Salim, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b who said: I said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "Some people of Madinah, when this verse in al-Baqarah about women's waiting periods was revealed, said: There remain categories of women's waiting periods not mentioned in the Qur'an: the young, the old whose menses have stopped, and the pregnant." He said: Then the shorter surah of al-Nisa' was revealed: ﴿And those of your women who have despaired of menstruation, if you are in doubt, their waiting period is three months, and those who have not menstruated﴾.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And for those who are pregnant, their term is until they deliver their burden﴾: Allah, the Exalted, says: whoever is pregnant, her waiting period ends with her delivery, even if that is immediately after the divorce or the death, as the consensus of the majority of scholars of the early and later generations holds, as is the explicit wording of this noble verse and as the Prophetic Sunnah has also reported. It has been narrated from Ali and Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that they held regarding a widow that she observes the longer of the two terms, delivery or the four months and ten days, acting upon this noble verse and the one in Surat al-Baqarah. al-Bukhari said:

Sa'd ibn Hafs related to us, Shayban related to us, from Yahya, who said: Abu Salamah informed me, who said: A man came to Ibn Abbas while Abu Hurayrah was sitting, and said: "Give me a ruling concerning a woman who gave birth forty nights after her husband." Ibn Abbas said: "The longer of the two terms." I said: ﴿And those who are pregnant, their term is until they deliver their burden﴾. Abu Hurayrah said: "I am with my nephew," meaning Abu Salamah. So Ibn Abbas sent his slave Kurayb to Umm Salamah to ask her. She said: "The husband of Subay'ah al-Aslamiyyah was killed while she was pregnant, and she gave birth forty nights after his death. Then she was proposed to, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ permitted her to marry, and Abu al-Sanabil was among those who proposed to her."

Thus al-Bukhari narrated this hadith here in abridged form. It has been narrated by him, Muslim, and the authors of the books in longer form through other chains [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4909); Sahih Muslim no. (1485); Sunan al-Nasa'i (6/191).]]. Imam Ahmad said:

Hammad ibn Usamah related to us, Hisham informed us, from his father, from al-Miswar ibn Makhramah: that Subay'ah al-Aslamiyyah's husband died while she was pregnant, and she did not remain but a few nights until she gave birth. When she was purified from her postnatal bleeding, she was proposed to, and she sought permission from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to marry, and he permitted her to marry, and she married.

It was narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, Muslim, Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah through various chains from her [[al-Musnad (4/327); Sahih al-Bukhari no. (5320); Sunan al-Nasa'i (6/190); Sunan Ibn Majah no. (2092), all from this chain narrated by Imam Ahmad. As for Muslim and Abu Dawud, it is the following chain, Sahih Muslim no. (1484); Sunan Abi Dawud no. (2306).]] as Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj said:

Abu al-Tahir related to me, Ibn Wahb informed us, Yunus ibn Yazid related to me, from Ibn Shihab, Ubayd Allah ibn Abd Allah ibn Utbah related to me: that his father wrote to Umar ibn Abd Allah ibn al-Arqam al-Zuhri, instructing him to visit Subay'ah bint al-Harith al-Aslamiyyah, ask her about her account and what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to her when she asked him for a ruling. Umar ibn Abd Allah wrote back informing him that Subay'ah told him that she had been married to Sa'd ibn Khawlah, who was among those who fought at Badr, and he died while she was pregnant during the Farewell Pilgrimage. She had hardly delivered her child after his death when, once she was purified from her postnatal bleeding, she adorned herself for suitors. Abu al-Sanabil ibn Ba'kak entered upon her and said: "Why do I see you adorned? Perhaps you hope to marry. By Allah, you will not marry until four months and ten days have passed over you." Subay'ah said: "When he said that to me, I gathered my clothes around me in the evening and came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and asked him about it, and he ruled that I had become free when I delivered my child, and commanded me to marry if I wished."

This is the wording of Muslim. Al-Bukhari narrated it in abridged form [[Sahih Muslim no. (1484); Sahih al-Bukhari no. (5319, 3991).]]. Then al-Bukhari, after narrating the first hadith at this verse, said:

Sulayman ibn Harb and Abu al-Nu'man said: Hammad ibn Zayd related to us, from Ayyub, from Muhammad, namely Ibn Sirin, who said: "I was in a circle in which was Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, may Allah have mercy on him, and his companions revered him. He mentioned the longer of the two terms, so I related the hadith of Subay'ah bint al-Harith from Abd Allah ibn Utbah." He said: "Some of his companions nudged me, and Muhammad said: I became wary of him, so I said to him: 'I would be bold to lie about Abd Allah while he is in a far corner of Kufah.'" He said: "He became embarrassed and said: 'But his paternal uncle did not say that.' Then I met Abu Atiyyah Malik ibn Amir and asked him, and he began to relate to me the hadith of Subay'ah. I said: 'Did you hear anything from Abd Allah?' He said: 'We were with Abd Allah, and he said: "Do you impose the strictness on her and not the leniency? The shorter sura of al-Nisa' was revealed after the longer: ﴿And those who are pregnant, their term is until they deliver their burden﴾.""

Ibn Jarir narrated it through the chain of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah and Isma'il ibn Ulayyah, from Ayyub, in abridged form [[Tafsir al-Tabari (28/92).]]. al-Nasa'i narrated it in his Tafsir from Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la, from Khalid ibn al-Harith, from Ibn Awn, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, and mentioned it [[It is in Sunan al-Nasa'i (6/196), and I did not find it in al-Kubra.]].

Ibn Jarir said: Zakariyya ibn Yahya ibn Aban al-Misri related to me, Sa'id ibn Abi Maryam related to us, Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, Ibn Shubrumah al-Kufi related to me, from Ibrahim, from Alqamah ibn Qays: that Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud said: "Whoever wishes, I will invoke a curse upon him: ﴿And those who are pregnant, their term is until they deliver their burden﴾ was not revealed except after the verse about the widow." He said: "And when a widow delivers, she is free." He meant by the verse about the widow: ﴿And those of you who die and leave wives, they shall wait by themselves for four months and ten days﴾ [al-Baqarah: 234].

al-Nasa'i narrated it from the hadith of Sa'id ibn Abi Maryam, with this chain [[Tafsir al-Tabari (28/92); Sunan al-Nasa'i (6/197).]]. Then Ibn Jarir said:

Ahmad ibn Mani' related to us, Muhammad ibn Ubayd related to us, Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid related to us, from al-Sha'bi, who said: "The longer of the two terms was mentioned in the presence of Ibn Mas'ud, and he said: 'Whoever wishes, I will swear to him by Allah that this verse in al-Nisa' the shorter was revealed after the four months and ten days.' Then he said: 'The term of the pregnant woman is that she delivers what is in her womb.'" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (28/92).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan al-Wasiti related to us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi related to us, from Sufyan, from al-A'mash, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, who said: "It reached Ibn Mas'ud that Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, was saying: 'The longer of the two terms.' He said: 'Whoever wishes, I will invoke a curse upon him: the verse in al-Nisa' the shorter was revealed after al-Baqarah: ﴿And those who are pregnant, their term is until they deliver their burden﴾."

Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah also narrated it from the hadith of Abu Mu'awiyah, from al-A'mash [[Sunan Abi Dawud no. (2307); Sunan Ibn Majah no. (2030).]].

Abd Allah ibn Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr al-Muqaddami related to me, Abd al-Wahhab al-Thaqafi informed us, al-Muthanna related to us, from Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from Abd Allah ibn Amr, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b who said: "I said to the Prophet ﷺ: '﴿And those who are pregnant, their term is until they deliver their burden﴾: is it the woman divorced three times or the widow?' He said: 'It is the woman divorced three times and the widow.'" [[Zawa'id al-Musnad (5/116).]]

This is an extremely strange hadith, indeed rejected (munkar), because in its chain is al-Muthanna ibn al-Sabbah, who is entirely abandoned in hadith. However, Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it with another chain, saying:

Muhammad ibn Dawud al-Simnani related to us, Amr ibn Khalid, namely al-Harrani, related to us, Ibn Lahi'ah related to us, from Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, that when this verse was revealed he said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "I do not know whether it is shared (mushtarakah) or unspecified (mubhamah)." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Which verse?" He said: "﴿Their term is until they deliver their burden﴾: the widow and the divorced?" He said: "Yes."

Ibn Jarir also narrated it in the same way from Abu Kurayb, from Musa ibn Dawud, from Ibn Lahi'ah. Then he narrated it again from Abu Kurayb, from Malik ibn Isma'il, from Ibn Uyaynah, from Abd al-Karim ibn Abi al-Mukharik that he related from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: "I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about: ﴿And those who are pregnant, their term is until they deliver their burden﴾." He said: "Yes, every pregnant woman's term is that she delivers what is in her womb." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (28/93). Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in al-Fath (8/654) after citing this narration: "Although none of its chains is free from criticism, the multiplicity of its routes indicates that it has a basis, and the story of Subay'ah supports it."]]

Abd al-Karim here is weak, and he did not meet Ubayy.

Ibn Kathir's commentary (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on Surah 65, verses 6–7:

Allah, the Exalted, says, commanding His servants: when one of them divorces a woman, he should house her in a dwelling until her 'iddah (the waiting period) ends. So He said: ﴿House them where you dwell﴾, that is, where you live, ﴿according to your means﴾. Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid and others said: that is, according to your capacity. Qatadah even said: if you find only the side of your house, then house her there.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And do not harm them in order to constrict them﴾. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: that is, he harasses her so that she will ransom herself from him with her wealth or leave his residence.

al-Thawri narrated from Mansur, from Abu al-Duha, concerning ﴿And do not harm them in order to constrict them﴾: he said, he divorces her, and when two days remain, he takes her back.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And if they are pregnant, then spend on them until they give birth﴾. Many scholars, among them Ibn 'Abbas, a group of the early generations (al-salaf), and groups of later scholars (al-khalaf), said: this applies to the irrevocably divorced woman (al-ba'in). If she is pregnant, he spends on her until she gives birth. They said: the evidence is that the revocably divorced woman (al-raj'iyyah) is owed maintenance whether she is pregnant or not.

Others said: rather, the whole context concerns revocable divorcees, and the mention of spending on the pregnant woman, even if she is revocable, is because pregnancy often lasts a long time. Thus it was necessary to state explicitly that maintenance is owed until delivery, lest one suppose that maintenance is owed only for the duration of the 'iddah.

The scholars differed: is the maintenance for her by means of the pregnancy, or for the pregnancy alone? There are two explicitly stated opinions from al-Shafi'i and others, and matters branch from them that are mentioned in the science of furu' (positive law).

* *

And His saying: ﴿And if they nurse for you﴾, that is, when they have given birth to their children while they are divorced, they have become irrevocably separated by the completion of their 'iddah. At that point she may nurse the child, and she may refrain from doing so. But after she gives him al-laba' (colostrum), which is the first milk, without which the child generally cannot survive. If she nurses, she is entitled to the wage of her equivalent (ajr mithlaha). She may contract with the father or his guardian on whatever wage they agree upon. For this reason Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿then give them their wages﴾. And His saying: ﴿And confer among yourselves in kindness﴾, that is, let your affairs among yourselves be conducted in kindness, without harm or injury, as Allah, the Exalted, said in Surah al-Baqarah: ﴿No mother should be harmed through her child, nor a father through his child﴾ [al-Baqarah: 233].

* *

And His saying: ﴿But if you disagree, then another woman will nurse for him﴾, that is, if the man and the woman disagree, and the woman demands a large wage for nursing and the man does not agree to it, or the man offers a small amount and she does not accept it, then let him hire another woman to nurse for him. If the mother agrees to what the outside woman was hired for, then she has more right to her child.

* *

And His saying: ﴿Let one of ample means spend from his ampleness﴾, that is, let his father or guardian spend on the infant according to his ability. ﴿And he whose provision is restricted, let him spend from what Allah has given him. Allah does not burden a soul beyond what He has given it﴾, like His saying: ﴿Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity﴾ [al-Baqarah: 286].

Ibn Jarir narrated: Ibn Humayd related to us, Hakkam related to us, from Abu Sinan, who said: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab asked about Abu 'Ubaydah. It was said that he wears coarse clothing and eats the roughest food. So he sent him a thousand dinars and said to the messenger: observe what he does with them when he takes them. Another had ten ounces, and he gave one ounce in charity. Another had one hundred ounces, and he gave ten ounces in charity." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "They are equal in reward, each has given a tenth of his wealth." Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Let one of ample means spend from his ampleness﴾. [al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (3/292); its chain is weak and broken, as mentioned several times before.]

This is a gharib (unusual) hadith from this route.

And His saying: ﴿Allah will bring about ease after hardship﴾. This is a promise from Him, the Exalted, and His promise is true; He does not break it. This is like His saying: ﴿So indeed with hardship is ease. Indeed with hardship is ease﴾ [al-Sharh: 5–6].

Imam Ahmad has narrated a hadith worth mentioning here. He said: Hashim ibn al-Qasim related to us, 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Bahram related to us, Shahr ibn Hawshab related to us, who said: Abu Hurayrah said: In former times a man and his wife were unable to obtain anything. The man came back from a journey and entered upon his wife, hungry and suffering from severe hunger. He said to his wife: Do you have anything? She said: Yes, rejoice, the provision of Allah has come to you. He urged her, and said: Woe to you! Seek, if you have anything. She said: Yes, a moment, hoping for the mercy of Allah. When his hunger lengthened, he said: Woe to you! Get up and seek, if you have anything, and bring it to me, for I have been exhausted and have endured hardship. She said: Yes, now the oven is being heated, so do not hurry. When he was silent for a while and she waited for him to speak to her, she said of her own accord: What if I got up and looked at my oven? She got up and looked at her oven, and it was full of sheep's ribs, and her millstones were grinding. She got up to the millstone and shook it, and took out what was in her oven of the sheep's ribs.

He also said in another place: Abu 'Amir related to us, Abu Bakr related to us, from Hisham, from Muhammad, who is Ibn Sirin, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: A man entered upon his family, and when he saw the need they were in, he went out into the desert. When his wife saw this, she got up to the millstone and set it going, and to the oven and heated it, then said: O Allah, provide for us. She looked, and the trough had become full. She went to the oven and found it full. He said: The husband came back and said: Have you found anything after me? His wife said: Yes, from our Lord. He went to the millstone and mentioned that to the Prophet (ﷺ), and the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, if you had not lifted it, it would have continued to turn until the Day of Resurrection." [al-Musnad (2/513).]

﴿So it tasted the evil consequence of its affair﴾, meaning: the outcome of its opposition, and they regretted when regret no longer benefited them. ﴿And the outcome of its affair was loss. Allah has prepared for them a severe punishment﴾, meaning: in the Hereafter, in addition to what He hastened for them in this world.

Then, after recounting the report of these people, He said: ﴿So fear Allah, O you of understanding (ulul-albab), who have believed﴾, meaning: O people of sound understanding, do not be like them, lest there befall you what befell them. ﴿O people of understanding who have believed﴾, meaning: who affirmed Allah and His messengers. ﴿Allah has certainly sent down to you a reminder (dhikr)﴾, meaning: the Qur'an. Allah, the Exalted, says, informing of His complete power and great dominion, so that this will move people to honour the upright religion He has prescribed:

﴿Allah is the One who created seven heavens﴾. This is like His saying, relating what Nuh (Noah) said to his people: ﴿Do you not see how Allah created seven heavens in layers?﴾ [Nuh: 15]. And He says: ﴿The seven heavens and the earth and whoever is in them glorify Him﴾ [al-Isra: 44].

His saying ﴿and of the earth, the like thereof﴾ means seven as well, as is established in the two Sahihs (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim): "Whoever usurps a span of land, it will be collared on him from seven earths" [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (2453) and Sahih Muslim no. (1612), from the hadith of 'Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her]]. And in Sahih al-Bukhari: "He will be swallowed down to seven earths" [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (3454), from the hadith of Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him]]. Its routes, wordings and attribution have been mentioned at the beginning of al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah (The Beginning and the End), in the passage on the creation of the earth, and to Allah belongs all praise and grace.

Whoever interprets this as seven climates has gone far from the point, delved too deeply into speculation, and contradicted the Qur'an and the hadith without any basis.

Earlier, in Surah al-Hadid, at His saying ﴿He is the First and the Last, and the Manifest and the Hidden﴾ [al-Hadid: 3], he mentioned the seven earths, the distance between them, and the thickness of each one being five hundred years. Ibn Mas'ud and others said likewise. Similarly, in another hadith: "The seven heavens and what is in them and between them, and the seven earths and what is in them and between them, compared to the Kursi (Footstool) are no more than a ring thrown down in a desert land" [[This hadith has already been referenced under the commentary on verse 255 of Surah al-Baqarah]].

Ibn Jarir said: Amr ibn 'Ali narrated to us, Waki' narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Muhajir, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿seven heavens and of the earth the like thereof﴾: He said, "If I were to tell you its explanation, you would disbelieve, and your disbelief would be your denial of it."

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, Ya'qub ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Sa'd al-Qummi al-Ash'ari narrated to us, from Ja'far ibn Abi al-Mughirah al-Khuza'i, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: A man said to Ibn 'Abbas, ﴿Allah is the One who created seven heavens and of the earth the like thereof﴾, the verse... Ibn 'Abbas said, "What assurance do you have that if I tell you about it, you will not disbelieve?"

Ibn Jarir also said: Amr ibn 'Ali and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, both saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Amr ibn Murrah, from Abu al-Duha, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding this verse, ﴿Allah is the One who created seven heavens and of the earth the like thereof﴾. He said: Amr said, he said: "In every earth there is an Ibrahim (Abraham), and the like of what is on the earth of creatures."

Ibn al-Muthanna said in his narration: "In every heaven, an Ibrahim." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (28/99)]] Al-Bayhaqi also narrated this report from Ibn 'Abbas in more detail than this context, in his book al-Asma' wa al-Sifat (The Names and Attributes). He said: Abu 'Abd Allah al-Hafiz told us, Ahmad ibn Ya'qub told us, 'Ubayd ibn Ghannam al-Nakha'i told us, 'Ali ibn Hakim told us, Sharik told us, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Abu al-Duha, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: ﴿Allah is the One who created seven heavens and of the earth the like thereof﴾. He said: "Seven earths; in every earth there is a prophet like your prophet, and Adam like Adam, and Nuh like Nuh, and Ibrahim like Ibrahim, and 'Isa like 'Isa."

Then al-Bayhaqi narrated it from the hadith of Shu'bah, from Amr ibn Murrah, from Abu al-Duha, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, ﴿Allah is the One who created seven heavens and of the earth the like thereof﴾: He said, "In every earth there is the like of Ibrahim, peace be upon him."

Then al-Bayhaqi said: The isnad of this from Ibn 'Abbas is sahih, but it is shadh (anomalous) through Murrah; I do not know of any corroborating narration for Abu al-Duha on it. And Allah knows best.

The Imam Abu Bakr 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Abi al-Dunya al-Qurashi said in his book al-Tafakkur wa al-I'tibar (Reflection and Contemplation): Ishaq ibn Hatim al-Mada'ini narrated to me, Yahya ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from 'Uthman ibn Abi Dahras, who said: It reached me that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to his companions while they were silent, not speaking. He said: "What is wrong with you that you do not speak?" They said: "Rather, we are reflecting on the creation of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic." He said: "Then do likewise: reflect on the creation of Allah, but do not reflect on Allah Himself, for in this West there is a white land, its light... – or he said its expanse – its light... – or he said its whiteness – its light, a journey of forty days for the sun, in which are creatures of Allah, the Exalted, who have never disobeyed Allah for the blink of an eye." They said: "Then where is the Shaytan (Satan) with respect to them?" He said: "They do not know whether Shaytan was created or was not created." They said: "Is he from the children of Adam?" He said: "They do not know whether Adam was created or was not created."

[[The hadith was mentioned by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur (2/408) and attributed by him to Ibn Abi al-Dunya]]

This is a mursal hadith, and it is extremely munkar (rejected). 'Uthman ibn Abi Dahrash was mentioned by Ibn Abi Hatim in his book, where he said: He narrated from a man from the family of al-Hakam ibn Abi al-'As, and from him narrated Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, Yahya ibn Sulaym al-Ta'ifi, and Ibn al-Mubarak. I heard my father say that. [[al-Jarh wa al-Ta'dil (6/149)]]
